limitations: No Digital Macaroni calendar connection, booking, payment, team routing, billing, or support test was completed.
The release date represents the verified TidyCal 2.0 public release record.

claims.statement: TidyCal creates booking pages, checks connected calendars, accepts paid bookings, and supports individual and team scheduling.
Low cost, basic setup, calendar sync, and simple booking links are the main positive patterns.
Customization, team depth, integration reliability, and booking failures are the key reported limits.
Free costs $0. Individual Lifetime costs $29 once. Agency Lifetime costs $79 once. Pro costs $12 monthly or $99 yearly.
Paid bookings add a 1% TidyCal platform fee to the booker's total, in addition to payment processing fees.

scoreRationale.onboarding: A booking page looks simple to create, but calendar choice, time zones, notices, buffers, and messages must be tested together.
scoreRationale.product: A strong low-cost option for a solo calendar and basic teams; reliability matters more than its broad feature list.
scoreRationale.support: Public feedback is mixed and no request was tested; Pro alone includes priority support.
scoreRationale.billing: The free and lifetime offers are unusually inexpensive, while Pro, paid-booking fees, and plan changes require a current comparison.
scoreRationale.overall: Run twenty booking attempts across every real route, including conflicts, time zones, payment, rescheduling, cancellation, and team assignment. Keep it only if nobody can book a time that should be closed.

conflictsAndUnknowns: A cheap lifetime plan lowers cost and does not reduce the harm of one bad booking.
More calendar connections simplify availability and create more places for sync to fail.
Team routing saves manual assignment only when calendars and priority rules remain correct.
No hands-on booking, payment, failure recovery, billing, or support test was completed.
